name: Defender — High-Confidence Endpoint/Identity/Office Attack Alert
description:
Attacker objective
Establish or extend a foothold — exploit a public-facing service, deliver malware, create a rogue account, or compromise an identity — surfaced by Microsoft Defender XDR (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365).

Attack logic
Defender's Endpoint/Identity/Office sensors apply cloud-scale analytics and raise a discrete alert on genuine attacker activity. Unlike the DLP and bulk-antivirus streams, these three sources correspond to real intrusion behaviour and are low-volume.

Why this detection works
Scoping to the Endpoint/Identity/Office sources (excluding DLP/bulk-AV and resolved alerts) surfaces every high-confidence Defender detection, and derives the device short-name and user so the alert can be correlated with Windows, AD and perimeter detections on the same entity.

False positives
A Defender benign-positive or a sanctioned red-team exercise (e.g. an authorised scanner triggering an exploitation alert).

Tuning
Triage against the Defender determination; suppress verified benign detections by title or actor; escalate high severity and privileged-user/critical-server alerts.

Required telemetry
m365_defender.alert (detection_source, severity, status, title, evidence.device_dns_name, user.name, threat.tactic.name).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Open the Defender alert and review the title, evidence entities and MITRE techniques.
2. Identify the device/user; for exploitation or account-creation alerts, treat the entity as compromised pending triage.
3. Correlate with the Windows/AD and perimeter detections on the same user/host.
false_positives: A Defender benign-positive or a sanctioned red-team exercise (e.g. an authorised scanner triggering an exploitation alert).
query:
FROM logs-m365_defender.alert* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE m365_defender.alert.detection_source IN ("microsoftDefenderForEndpoint","microsoftDefenderForIdentity","microsoftDefenderForOffice365") AND m365_defender.alert.severity != "informational" AND m365_defender.alert.status != "resolved" AND NOT user.name IN ("nessus")
| EVAL host.name = MV_FIRST(SPLIT(TO_LOWER(MV_FIRST(m365_defender.alert.evidence.device_dns_name)), "."))
| KEEP @timestamp, user.name, host.name, m365_defender.alert.title, m365_defender.alert.severity, m365_defender.alert.detection_source, m365_defender.alert.incident_id, threat.tactic.name, m365_defender.alert.evidence.device_dns_name
